finding.claim: The /logo handler fetches an attacker-supplied URL. Its only validation is a substring check for "example.io" on the raw string, not on the parsed host. An attacker can reach internal hosts or cloud metadata with URLs such as http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/?x=example.io, http://evil.com/example.io, or http://example.io@127.0.0.1:8081/. The default http.Get client follows redirects, and the response body is returned to the attacker, so this is full-read SSRF.
finding.source: r.FormValue("logo") (query or form parameter on the unauthenticated /logo route)
finding.sink: http.Get(raw) at main.go:36, with the response body copied back to the client via io.Copy at main.go:38

trace.note: /logo is registered with no auth guard
raw is taken directly from the request
strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") is the only check, applied to the string rather than the parsed host
http.Get(raw) uses the default client, which follows redirects and has no IP or scheme restrictions
the response body is streamed back to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: Substring check only (bypassable via path, query, userinfo or subdomain). No scheme allowlist. No parsed-host comparison. No private, loopback or link-local IP blocking. No DNS pinning. Redirects are followed by default. No auth middleware.

verdict.guard_found: none (only strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") at main.go:32, a substring check that does not close the finding)
verdict.reason: The trace entry for /logo registration is wrong: main.go:42 registers /cdn and /logo is registered at main.go:43. The rest of the SSRF is real: main.go:31 takes the URL from the request, main.go:32 only does a substring check, main.go:36 calls http.Get with the default redirect-following client, and main.go:38 copies the response back. The REFUTED verdict rests only on this one-line trace error, so the finding should be resubmitted with the line corrected.
